newsitem.title: USA: Calif. banker fined over campaign gifts - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. banker fined over campaign gifts - report.

text.p: Calvin Grigsby, whose California firm is one of the largest African American-owned municipal bond underwriters in the United States, has paid a $5,000 fine over charges he violated state laws governing campaign contributions, a newspaper reported.

Neither Grigsby nor members of the state's Fair Political Practices Commission were available this weekend to comment on the report, published in Friday evening editions of The San Francisco Examiner.

According to the report, the commission found that Grigsby loaned $5,000 to an attorney in 1993 with the understanding she would donate it to Alameda County Supervisor Mary King, who was then running for mayor of Oakland, Calif.

The commission also found that Grigsby violated California's Fair Political Practices Act by failing to file required disclosure statements for the $53,500 he and Fiscal Funding, a firm he controls, gave to candidates in 1993, the newspaper said.
Grigsby's firm, Grigsby Brandford & Co of San Francisco, has underwritten more than $1 billion worth of bonds for Alameda County.
